label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Rick, I’m pissed, and I don’t want you to brush this off with “that’s business, sis, can’t win ’em all.” You promised Gary Pruitt I’d list his house off Ray Road in Chandler for 1% without ever asking me. My listing side is 2.5%. I have never quoted 1% to anyone, and you had no right to throw that number around as some “family rate.”

I spent Saturday, Nov. 7, pulling comps, doing the walkthrough, and printing a full listing packet. That was about six hours of work, plus the drive from north Phoenix. Then Sunday night Gary texted that he was going with ListLite for their $3,995 flat fee. I’m not really mad at Gary. He made his choice. I’m mad at you for volunteering my time, quoting my commission, and then acting like my wasted Saturday was no big deal. “Can’t win ’em all” is easy to say when you weren’t the one doing the work.

This isn’t the first time, either. The same thing happened with your softball friend two years ago, and I let it go. Now you’ve already given Denise my cell so she can “pick my brain” about selling her rental. I’m not calling Denise. You gave her my number, so you can tell her.

I’m happy to help actual family—Mom, your kids, any of us—with advice, and I won’t charge for that. But I’m done being the favor you hand out to friends and coworkers so you get to look like a big shot while I work for free.

So, to be clear: no more quoting my commission, promising my time, or handing out my number. Ask me first, every time. If I agree, then I’ll take it from there. This stops now.

I’m still coming to Thanksgiving, and I’m not trying to turn this into some huge family war. I love you. But I need you to actually hear me and respect this.
